newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP to develop new iron ore mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP to develop new iron ore mine.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday its BHP Iron Ore unit would develop the Orebody 18 mine in the Pilbara region of Western Australia.
BHP said the A$96 million development of the mine was planned to start in March 1997 and would be full production from mid-1998.
BHP said Orebody 18, 32 km east of Newman in the Pilbara region of Western Australia, would be a satellite to the Mt Whaleback mine.

It would produce five million tonnes a year initially, increasing over several years to 10 million tonnes a year, BHP said. The total mineable reserve of Brockman hematite was estimated at 116 million tonnes.
The ore would be railed to Nelson Point in Port Hedland where it would be blended and stockpiled with ores from other mines in the Newman area.

BHP group general manager Geoff Wedlock said in a statement that development of Orebody 18 was an important contribution to plans to increase BHP Iron Ore's total shipments to more than 70 million tonnes a year in 1999 from an estimated 61 million tonnes in the financial year ending May 31, 1997.

"The introduction of Orebody 18 enables us to extend the life of our prime ore supply from the Mt Whaleback mine, achieve projected market demand and, because of the high grade of this ore, will enhance our ability to meed grade specifications," Wedlock said.

BHP said the development would include an eight km rail spur connecting the mine to the main Newman to Port Hedland railway; crushing, screening and trainloading facilities; a 35 km power line from BHP Iron Ore's gas-fired power station at Newman; and workforce accommodation in Newman.
The construction workforce would peak at about 150 people, and up to 100 people would be employed in operating the mine, BHP said.
